title: The Current of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Casper Underhill, a debt-ridden storm chaser hiding in the rain-shadow badlands of Patagonia, is hired to find a missing government survey team. He discovers the team alive but guarding an underground aquifer vast enough to make or break nations—and the 'dangerous optimists' he owes money to are already moving to seize it. To bring the surveyors home, Casper must betray either his creditors or the truth, and he chooses a third path: faking the expedition's failure while smuggling its evidence to the one journalist who can be trusted. The book ends with Casper testifying under his own name for the first time in twelve years, the aquifer protected by law, and his debts settled not with money but with testimony.
about_author: Theo Whitlock is the pen name of a former field hydrologist who spent six years mapping water rights across South America before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels where landscapes keep better secrets than people do.

chapters.title: Rain Shadow
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Establishes the dry side of Patagonia, Casper's weather instruments, and the ledger of debts he keeps taped inside his truck visor. A collector named Ferro finds him at a fuel stop and gives him two weeks. Emotional beat: claustrophobic normalcy about to crack.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A government liaison offers triple his rate to locate Survey Team Kestrel—six people, eleven days overdue, gear intact at their last camp but no tracks leading out. Casper takes the job because refusing means Ferro collects. Beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Gear With No Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the abandoned camp he finds tents pitched, food cached, and a seismograph still running on battery—pointing at something below. One boot print heads toward the mesas and simply stops. Beat: first true dread.

chapters.title: Ferro's Optimists
chapters.summary: POV Marisol Ferro. Reveals her syndicate's interest: they financed Kestrel's original permit through shell companies and need the survey results before anyone else reads them. Beat: the antagonist's reasonable, chilling logic.

chapters.title: Into the Badlands
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Three days of driving into terrain that eats vehicles, tracking anomalies in wind data that suggest a microclimate—cool air rising from nowhere. Beat: wonder reawakening the scientist he buried.

chapters.title: The Breathing Ground
chapters.summary: POV Casper. He finds a sinkhole breathing fog at dawn and hears voices below. First contact with Kestrel's scout, Ilsa Reyes, who holds him at arrow-point until he proves he isn't Ferro's. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Found
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Flashback woven with present: the team fell into a cavern system over a fossil aquifer—a freshwater sea older than the Andes' last uplift. Their leader, Dr. Okafor, ordered silence until they understood what they'd found. Beat: awe shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Around the campfire, Ilsa asks why a man with his skills hides in the driest place on earth. He tells half the story: a flood forecast he falsified under pressure, a town that drowned, a name he shed. Beat: confession as currency.

chapters.title: The Extraction Problem
chapters.summary: POV Dr. Okafor. She refuses to leave: six of her team are injured or sick from contaminated seep water, but moving them exposes the site. Casper argues they're all dead if Ferro's crews arrive first. Beat: leadership vs. survival, loyalty vs. truth begins.

chapters.title: Dust on the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Satellite phone intercept confirms Ferro has dispatched a 'rescue' convoy—armed, well-funded, carrying drilling permits signed by a bribed minister. Two days out. Beat: clock starts hammering.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ferro. She calls Casper directly: bring out the survey data and his debts vanish; bring out nothing and she'll bury him with the team. He agrees aloud while planning otherwise. Beat: the lie that defines him.

chapters.title: Carrying the Wounded
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Improvised litters, a two-day trek to the trucks, a sandstorm as cover. Ilsa notices Casper navigating by instinct no storm chaser should have—he's been here before, years ago, chasing something else. Beat: trust deepening through labor.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Ferro's advance men stop the convoy. Casper hands over a decoy drive of doctored data showing the aquifer as brine-poisoned and worthless. The men radio confirmation north. Beat: gambit made, no way back.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She saw the real data; she knows the decoy is false, and now Casper has lied to armed men on her behalf—which makes her complicit. Confrontation at night: why should she trust a man who admits to falsifying forecasts? Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns inward.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Dr. Okafor. She reveals she knew about Ferro's financing all along and stayed silent to protect funding—her silence helped build this trap. She decides the data goes public, even if it ends her career. Beat: power examined from inside.

chapters.title: The Long Drive North
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Convoy races toward Esquel, pursued by Ferro's second team who've realized the decoy doesn't match seismic records. Truck breaks an axle; they trade a wounded man's comfort for speed. Beat: attrition and resolve.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ferro's men box them in a canyon. Casper uses storm-chasing craft—reading wind, timing a dust wall—to slip the net, but Ilsa is shot covering the retreat. Beat: cost of the third path.

chapters.title: What Water Is Worth
chapters.summary: POV Ferro. Her syndicate fractures: some want to sell the aquifer quietly, others to hold a nation's agriculture hostage. She realizes Casper played her and sets a price on him. Beat: corruption devouring its own.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In Esquel they reach Elena Brandt, the reporter Casper has fed small truths to for years without giving his name. Hospital-bound Ilsa delivers the real data. Beat: handing off the burden of truth.

chapters.title: Two Weeks Due
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Ferro's collectors corner him at the same fuel stop where the book began. Instead of running, he walks into their car and asks to be taken to her. Beat: courage as choosing consequence.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Before a parliamentary commission—and with Ferro arrested mid-bribe—Casper gives his full name, his old crime, and the aquifer's coordinates into public record. Truth as the only debt he can finally pay. Beat: climax and catharsis.

chapters.title: First Rain
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Months later: the aquifer protected by statute, Kestrel's survivors scattered but bound, Casper staying on as the reserve's first warden. Rain falls on the dry side—rare, unremarkable, enough. Beat: found family, quiet resolution.
